correctness.rationale: The last three conditions are precisely the cover requirement. Two omitted leaves on one side give indistinguishable pendant edges, since all other vertices reach both edges via the shared center. Conversely a selected leaf separates same-side pendant edges; a selected center separates opposite-side pendant edges; and the central edge is separated from a pendant edge by the opposite center or, if it is omitted, any of its forced selected leaves. For an independent count, regard the complement of the generator as the omitted vertices. No more than two can be omitted. The valid two-element omissions are a pair of opposite leaves (pq), or one center and a leaf on the opposite side (p+q). All p+q+2 single omissions and the empty omission work. This proves the polynomial and minima for every p,q>=1, including p=q=1. A separate distance-based enumeration tested 3,600 subsets over 1<=p,q<=4 and agreed on both set feasibility and coefficients.
residual_risks: The independent and bundled enumerations cover finite boxes only. The claim excludes zero-leaf sides; the separation proof uses a nonempty opposite leaf set.

evidence: Remark 3's necessity applies to every edge generator in a nonpath tree, and the construction gives an edge generator by choosing all but one terminal leaf at each applicable vertex.

broader_coverage.reasoning: This is stronger evidence than a matching minimum formula. For two branching centers, the ordinary theorem and monotonicity characterize every edge generator, after which imposing the cover condition is an exact intersection. The uniform-corona formula alone would not settle the unbalanced all-set claim.

evidence: For p,q>=2 all leaves on the two sides are exactly the relevant legs. A set with at most one omitted leaf per side contains a previously constructed ordinary generator (choose exactly p−1 and q−1 among the available leaves); the necessary condition is already in the same proof. Intersect with the cover rule and count the three possible kinds of omitted pairs to obtain the entire polynomial in that regime.

For p=1<q, the long leg at v has vertices u,a_1. On a cover it is occupied. The only issue with using the earlier leaf-only construction is if a_1 is omitted and u is selected; substituting u for a_1 preserves its comparisons between edges other than ua_1, since all those distances decrease by one, and the cover separates ua_1 from uv via v or any selected B-leaf. The path p=q=1 is a direct three-edge check.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The boundary checks finish correctness but do not leave a substantial original theorem after the main structural claim and coefficients are accounted for. The conclusion is not based on a keyword miss or on the already known balanced minimum alone.

originality.rationale: Although no literal double-star enumerator was found, the central all-set claim for arbitrary p,q>=2 follows mechanically from the existing all-but-one-legs necessity and leaf-generator construction for ordinary edge resolution in Kelenc–Tratnik–Yero, Remark 3 and its proof, together with Tavakoli et al.'s cover definition. This covers unbalanced as well as balanced stars in the two-branching-center regime. The polynomial there is just the count of allowed omissions under that criterion, not an independent invariant calculation. The one-leaf boundary is not expressly covered by the leaf-only construction, so this is not a claim that every frozen sentence was previously published; the boundary adds only a routine adjustment and does not salvage the assigned finding as an original contribution.
residual_risks: An explicit earlier published double-star enumerator was not located. The implication assessment relies on the actual ordinary tree proof and the cover intersection, not a claim of literal publication of the polynomial.
